evidence.source: Shuowen.org, entry for 睡, reproducing Shuowen and Duan Yucai’s commentary
evidence.field: definition; graphic analysis; cited literary examples
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen gloss “坐寐也。从目、垂” (“sleep while sitting; from 目 and 垂”). Duan Yucai says the eyes droop, and notes that the Song edition lacks 聲 (“sound”), so the analysis combines semantic interpretation with phonetic structure. He cites 左傳 “坐而假寐” and 戰國策 “讀書欲睡.” These citations attest the word in the texts as transmitted, but do not independently date surviving manuscripts.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text and later commentary
evidence.title: 說文解字「睡」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, entry A00764 垂
evidence.text: The entry reports the Shuowen form of 垂 as “遠邊也。从土 [phonetic element] 聲” (“distant boundary; from 土, with [the remaining element] as phonetic”). It also distinguishes historical and later variants of 垂, including forms described as vulgar or erroneous. This supports a phonetic analysis of 垂 itself, while not establishing the original referent of its phonetic element.
evidence.title: A00764 垂 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, entry A00764 垂
evidence.text: The entry describes several written forms as variants and reports that one form was called a vulgar error. This indicates that graphic variation and corruption were recognized in the transmission of 垂-related forms; it does not show that 睡 itself arose through corruption.
evidence.title: A00764 垂 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Baxter–Sagart 2014 table supplied in local primary readings
evidence.text: The provided exact row records 睡 with MC dzyweH and OC *[d]o[j]-s, glossed “doze off.” These are Baxter–Sagart table readings, distinct from other reconstruction systems. The corresponding 垂 row was not supplied, so this local evidence alone does not establish a same-system sound comparison.

gaps: No verified oracle-bone, bronze, or securely dated early manuscript form of 睡 was located in this search pass; the graph’s earliest physical attestation and detailed graphic evolution therefore remain open.

The Shuowen gloss “sleep while sitting” and cited Zuozhuan/Strategies of the Warring States examples provide an early lexical framing, but this research did not establish the texts’ manuscript dates or a chronology from “sit/doze” to broader sleep senses.

The phonetic role of 垂 is supported by the Shuowen commentator’s explicit sound-component observation and sound-series context, but the exact current Mandarin kMandarin reading of 垂 and an exact local Baxter–Sagart row for 垂 were not available for this task; no same-system numeric comparison is asserted.

The Unihan pages for both inspected characters were inaccessible despite direct URL attempts. The provided local 睡 readings are records from the specified local sources, not independently verified upstream page contents.
No evidence found that 睡 is a whole-graph phonetic loan, or that its graphic structure is corrupt. Evidence about variant or erroneous forms of 垂 does not establish corruption in 睡.
